claims.text: A multiscale simulation framework can integrate phase-field modeling, crystal plasticity, and calibrated interatomic potentials.
The integrated framework can concurrently predict and optimize phase stability in multiphase alloys.
The integrated framework can refine alloy microstructure under severe deformation and thermal processing.
The integrated framework can enhance material properties under severe deformation and thermal processing.
Calibrated interatomic potentials can reproduce structural properties and relative phase stability in a high-entropy alloy.
High-strain deformation can promote atomistic rearrangements in a high-entropy alloy.
Phase transformation and recrystallization mechanisms are active under the proposed high-strain, high-temperature conditions.
Coupling phase-field transformations with plastic deformation produces controlled phase evolution.
Coupling phase-field transformations with plastic deformation produces microstructural refinement.
Thermodynamic descriptors such as mixing enthalpy, atomic-size difference, and omega are related to single-phase formation in high-entropy alloys.
Tuning processing parameters through the proposed framework controls competing thermodynamic and kinetic factors.
Control of thermodynamic and kinetic factors simultaneously secures phase stability, refines microstructure, and optimizes properties.
The proposed intervention will produce a finer and more uniform microstructure than conventional processing.
The proposed intervention will improve mechanical properties relative to conventional processing.
Conventional processing adjusts phase stability, microstructure, and properties independently.
Independent adjustment by conventional processing often creates trade-offs among phase stability, microstructure, and properties.
Accurate calibration against experimental or first-principles data is necessary for the proposed framework's applicability.
Inadequate interatomic potentials or inaccurate treatment of nonequilibrium interfaces will reduce predictive accuracy.
The magnitudes of phase-stability enhancement, grain refinement, and property improvement are uncertain because of model-calibration uncertainty and material-specific behavior.
